Shell(cd /Users/0xboji/dev/app/terax-ai && gh issue create --title "fix(terminal): typed space followed by backspace corrupts the shell command on macOS" --body "## User impact Typing a command like \`mcli\` then **space, backspace, space** on macOS produces \`mcl \` (missing the \`i\`, plus an extra space) instead of \`mcli \`. Pasting the same text works fine. ## Root cause The macOS WebKit text bridge can store an intended space in xterm's textarea as a C1 control (U+0080–U+009F) or a Unicode space lookalike (NBSP U+00A0, thin/medium spaces, etc.) instead of a regular space. Two problems compound: 1. \`normalizeMacTerminalInput\` only collapsed the C1 range, so NBSP and other space lookalikes passed through unchanged. This is the root cause of \`git clone <url>\` typed by hand failing (\`git: 'clone <url>' is not a git command\`) while pasting worked. 2. \`writeDiff\` in \`macImeBridge.ts\` compared the raw textarea value against the stored \`lastValue\`. When the previous space was stored as C1/NBSP and the next keystroke arrived as a regular space, the common-prefix diff mismatched at that position and emitted a spurious DEL (\\x7f), deleting the character before the space and appending duplicates. ## Scope - \`src/modules/terminal/lib/macImeBridge.ts\`: normalize both sides of the diff, and broaden \`normalizeMacTerminalInput\` to all Unicode space lookalikes. - \`src/modules/terminal/lib/macImeBridge.test.ts\`: cover NBSP and C1-vs-space diff scenarios. ## Acceptance criteria - \`normalizeMacTerminalInput\` collapses C1 controls, NBSP, and other space lookalikes into a regular space. - \`writeDiff\` compares normalized values so a C1/NBSP space never diffs into a spurious DEL. - Typing \`mcli␣⌫␣\` yields \`mcli \` on macOS." 2>&1 | tail -5)

WebKit can store an intended space as a C1 control (U+0080-U+009F) or a Unicode space lookalike (NBSP, thin/medium spaces, ...) in xterm's textarea. normalizeMacTerminalInput only collapsed the C1 range, and writeDiff compared raw textarea values, so a C1/NBSP space followed by a regular space diffed into a spurious DEL that deleted the previous character. Normalize both sides of the diff before comparing and broaden the normalizer to every space lookalike the shell would not split on. Shell(cd /Users/0xboji/dev/app/terax-ai && gh issue create --title "fix(terminal): initial command sent twice breaks agent CLIs on Windows" --body "## User impact Opening a workspace that launches 4 terminal agent CLIs (e.g. via \`initialCommand\` on pane creation) intermittently leaves panes **empty with no prompt and no input response** on Windows 11 + pwsh. Roughly 1 in 4 agents is affected (race), and subsequent new panes in other workspaces also come up empty. ## Root cause The initial command is written to the PTY by **two independent paths that both fire on the first OSC 133 A prompt marker**: 1. **Rust** — \`InitialCommandBootstrap\` in \`src-tauri/src/modules/pty/session.rs\` waits for the \`ESC ] 133;A ESC \\\` marker, then writes the command. 2. **Frontend** — \`flushInitialCommand\` in \`src/modules/terminal/lib/useTerminalSession.ts\`, wired into \`registerPromptTracker\`'s \`onPrompt\` callback (also fired on OSC 133 A), writes the same command. A 900 ms \`scheduleInitialCommandFallback\` can write it a third time. Both fire on the same marker and never coordinate, so an agent CLI can receive the command twice while starting up → it wedges (empty TUI, no input echo). macOS masks it via timing; Windows pwsh's slower startup exposes it. ## Fix Remove the frontend write path entirely; **Rust is the single sender**. \`flushInitialCommand\` and \`scheduleInitialCommandFallback\` are deleted, and \`registerPromptTracker\` is called without the \`onPrompt\` flush callback. Agent metadata (pane chrome) is unaffected — \`ensureSession\` already calls \`setAgentCliCommand\` for known CLIs, and \`deliverPtyBytes\` auto-detects agent banners from output. Canvas terminals are unaffected (they rely solely on Rust bootstrap). ## Acceptance criteria - \`initialCommand\` is written to the PTY exactly once, by the Rust bootstrap. - Opening a workspace with 4 agent CLIs on Windows never produces an empty, unresponsive pane. - Existing agent-chrome tests still pass. ## Validation - \`pnpm vitest run src/modules/terminal src/modules/architecture\` — 76 passed - \`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit\` — clean - \`pnpm build\` — success - Manual verification on Windows (pwsh) pending." 2>&1 | tail -3)
